channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: Trump's weekend rallies in Kansas, Iowa are back on
item.description: The rallies were cancelled on Thursday.

item.title: Bugatti CEO chases down car thief - then offers him lift home
item.description: The head of the luxury car-maker Bugatti has promised to stop leaving his keys in his own car after his £2m model was stolen from a company site in Zagreb.

item.title: France braces for new wave of protests, govt warns of 'very high' violence risk
item.description: France's interior minister on Thursday warned of a "very high risk of public disorder" and announced the deployment of around 70,000 police officers for a new wave of protests this weekend. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, with nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerating into some of the country's worst rioting in years. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi tells us more.

item.title: Billionaire tax, transgender rights, voter access among key midterm ballot measures
item.description: Voters will weigh in on several key ballot measures in the midterm elections.

item.title: Black Sea shipping under growing threats as drones hit container ships
item.description: A Greek container ship has sunk after being struck by three drones, potentially of Russian origin, in the Black Sea off the Bulgarian coast on Wednesday, October 28. This incident highlights growing concerns for commercial shipping as the conflict between Ukraine and Russia persists.

item.title: 'The Phantom of the Opera' haunts French cinemas again
item.description: In this edition of arts24, "Le Fantôme de l'Opéra" returns to French cinemas in a contemporary reinterpretation starring Deva Cassel and Romain Duris. We take a closer look.

item.title: Spanish transport minister faces calls to quit after deadly train crash
item.description: Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente faced calls to resign but ruled out stepping down on Friday. This follows Wednesday’s train crash in Toledo province, which killed 69 people. It is the country’s second high-speed rail disaster this year. FRANCE 24 correspondent Sarah Morris reports.

item.title: Third weekend of protests looms as tensions persist across France
item.description: For the third Saturday in a row, people across France are set to take to the streets to protest against the high cost of living and demand better funding for education. Police are preparing for all eventualities ahead of another weekend of protests, following earlier demonstrations that ended in rioting and looting in city centres.

item.title: Who is Kevin T., the main suspect behind the racist Trappes attack?
item.description: France's anti-terrorism prosecutor on Thursday released details of the main suspect in the racist attack in Trappes and La Verriere, on the outskirts of Paris, on October 23.The 39-year-old opened fire with a submachine gun, killing 26-year-old Pengo Bossio Wangi and injuring five others.

item.title: How will the women's vote shape the US midterms?
item.description: With the US midterms approaching, we examine the power of the women's vote in an election that will shape the balance of power in Washington during Donald Trump’s final two years in office. Annette Young talks to Annie Karni, congressional correspondent for The New York Times and Kelly Dittmar, Director of Research at the Centre for American Women and Politics.

item.title: How the record-breaking $6.3 billion heist in crypto history unfolded
item.description: Hackers stole $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance in a record-breaking heist, prompting issuers to freeze roughly half of the stolen assets. The breach, which US analysts suspect was done by North Korean hackers, has shaken confidence in the crypto market.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope in history to vote in a US election
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope in history to vote in a U.S. general election

item.title: Georgia's European dream left in limbo
item.description: Two years ago in Georgia, tens of thousands of pro-European protesters rallied against the disputed results of the October 2024 parliamentary election, which was officially won by the ruling Georgian Dream party. A few weeks later, the authorities announced the suspension of the country's European Union accession process. Despite an ongoing crackdown, smaller-scale protests continue every day in the capital Tbilisi.

item.title: Texas Republicans accused of changing electoral rules ahead of midterms
item.description: With the US midterm elections approaching, Republicans in Texas are being accused of changing electoral rules in their favour. In Tarrant County, near Dallas, they've cut the number of election-day polling places by nearly 30 percent. The decision is being challenged in court and adds to last year's state-wide redistricting, a move designed to benefit Republicans. But the measures could also help galvanise the Democratic opposition. FRANCE 24's Pierrick Leurent reports, with Wassim Cornet.

item.title: Dem wants to keep Trump from buying DC golf course after federally funded renovations
item.description: Rep. Huffman wants "guardrails" to keep the president from profiting from it.

item.title: WATCH: State of the race with 4 days until midterm vote
item.description: Nearly 45 million people have already turned out to vote, and those early voting numbers have surpassed where the numbers were at this point in the 2022 midterm election.

item.title: Meta, TikTok and X lose hearing against UK watchdog over moderation data demands
item.description: Meta, ‌TikTok and X have lost a legal challenge against ‌the UK's regulator over the amount of information it is demanding under new laws.

item.title: ‘Scared of crossing the border’: The Arizona farmers who rely on Mexican workers
item.description: The vast produce farms of Yuma County, Arizona, rely heavily on foreign workers who cross the border every day from Mexico. John Boelts, a farmer and staunch supporter of US President Donald Trump, praises the administration’s strict border controls – though he says that competing Republican factions have complicated efforts to hire foreign labourers.

item.title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after company given lowest environmental rating
item.description: Yorkshire Water has announced its chief executive is stepping down - a day after the company was given the lowest environmental rating by regulators.

item.title: DOJ issues grand jury subpoenas to election officials in California
item.description: DOJ issues grand jury subpoenas to local election officials in California as part of its investigation into the state’s voter rolls, multiple sources told ABC News.

item.title: Trump administration says biggest changes coming to infant formula in nearly 30 years
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration announced on Thursday it is proposing a new rule that will update the nutrient requirements for infant formula.

item.title: DOJ issues new wave of subpoenas in criminal probe of Alaska Senate race, sources say
item.description: The DOJ is issuing new subpoenas in a probe of Alaska's U.S. Senate race and alleged efforts by Democrats to recruit a candidate with the same name as the GOP incumbent.

item.title: Why is the Cheesecake Factory at the center of the latest culture war?
item.description: A joke by former President Obama has gone viral and received backlash from the Trump administration as the issue of affordability looms large over next week's midterm elections. (Image credit: Kayla Bartkowski)

item.title: AI-powered 'doorbell cameras' tested to alert people to approaching polar bears
item.description: Artificial intelligence-powered "doorbell cameras" are being tested by a team of international experts in Canada to warn communities about approaching polar bears as climate change increases the risk of dangerous encounters.

item.title: Banished: The Taliban's War On Women - tickets go live for Sky News documentary screening
item.description: Tickets are now on sale for a screening, followed by a Q&A, of Alex Crawford's new documentary, Banished: The Taliban's War On Women.

item.title: Russia recruits Africans to fight in Ukraine, families seek answers
item.description: While African leaders and Russian officials gather to discuss security, trade and political cooperation at the Africa-Russia summit, one sensitive issue is notably absent from the agenda: the recruitment of Africans to fight for Russia in Ukraine. More than 1,400 Africans have been enlisted since 2023. In Tunisia, concern is growing as the families of several men who travelled to Russia for work or study are still searching for answers about the fate of their loved ones. FRANCE 24's team in Tunisia reports.

item.title: What to know about the US economy as midterm elections near
item.description: The economy ranks as a top concern among voters as campaigns race toward the midterm elections early next month.

item.title: Foiled Hindu temple plot exposes rising anti-Indian sentiment in the US
item.description: In this edition of Access Asia, we explore why anti-Indian sentiment is rising in the United States in the wake of the foiled plot targeting a Hindu temple in Illinois. We ask the executive director of the Center for the Study of Organized Hate what's behind the trend, and whether the rhetoric coming from the Trump White House is to blame.

item.title: At least 60 Christians killed in Ethiopia amid rising religious violence
item.description: At least 60 Christians have been killed in Ethiopia in what the Orthodox Church has declared as religious violence. It is still unclear who was behind the attack, with rebels and local government blaming each other. Around 20 houses have been burned down, as FRANCE 24's correspondent Tom Canetti reports.

item.title: Senegal gears up for historic 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar
item.description: The International Olympic Committee is upbeat just 24 hours before competition gets under way at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal. Venues are ready to host the first-ever Olympic event on the African continent. FRANCE 24's correspondent Aminatou Diallo reports from the ground.

item.title: Tanzania: 2025 election violence still traumatises, one year on
item.description: Tanzania is marking the first anniversary of a bloody election that left many traumatised. The October 29, 2025 election, in which President Samia Suluhu Hassan won with 98 percent of the vote after most of the opposition was excluded, triggered days of protests that security forces brutally suppressed. Many government critics say they still fear abduction, arbitrary arrest and politically motivated prosecutions.

item.title: TotalEnergies posts record profits as it keeps a lid on fuel prices
item.description: As hundreds of thousands across France are expected to take to the street again this weekend to protest the high cost of living, oil and gas giant TotalEnergies has posted record profits for the quarter to September. The company has kept fuel prices lower than rivals at its pumps, but motorists are wondering whether it could bring them lower still.

item.title: Tennis: Alexander Zverev guaranteed to become world No. 1
item.description: Alexander Zverev secured his place as the next world No. 1 by beating Tallon Griekspoor (6-4, 7-5) at the ATP 500 tournament in Vienna. The 29-year-old German will top the ATP rankings on Monday, November 2, replacing Jannik Sinner. He will become the first German world No. 1 since Boris Becker in 1991, and the 30th player in history to reach the top spot.

item.title: Israel elections: Netanyahu attacks Arab parties as they emerge as potential kingmakers
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party alleged on Thursday, without ​providing evidence, that Arab parties' record gains in an election this week were driven in part by voter fraud. These accusations represent an escalation of anti-Arab rhetoric by Netanyahu and his far-right partners after Arab-led parties made a historic showing in the election – giving them a potential kingmaker role in the next government

item.title: Poundland bidder tells administrator it remains keen on rescue deal
item.description: The Northern Irish company attempting to stage a solvent rescue of Poundland has told the discount retailer's administrator-in-waiting that it remains keen on a deal which could save more than 10,000 jobs.

item.title: Israel elections: Difficult negotiations lie ahead after Netanyahu's bloc lost majority
item.description: Israel's final election results confirmed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc lost its majority of parliamentary seats and that weeks of difficult negotiations among very different parties, from ultra-Orthodox Jewish to secular to Arab-led, lie ahead. The results released early Friday showed Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday's elections. The main opposition bloc won 48. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle tells us more.

item.title: Spain demands answers as train disaster toll rises
item.description: Spain began demanding answers on Thursday after the toll from the country's second high-speed train collision this year rose to 69 people, with scores injured and distraught relatives desperately seeking news about their loved ones. One of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century struck south of Madrid on Wednesday morning when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.

item.title: Bomb squad called and homes evacuated after 'neighbour dispute'
item.description: Homes have been evacuated while a bomb squad examines "small items" found by police after a row between neighbours.

item.title: WATCH: Cruise cancels global trip over rising fuel costs, strands 200 passengers in Cambodia
item.description: Some passengers sold their home to live on the cruise ship full-time.

item.title: US midterms: With deep-red states now in play, could blue wave redraw America's political landscape?
item.description: With the US approaching a potentially consequential midterm election, the political landscape appears to be shifting. Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Dr Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics & Policy at Queen Mary University of London, who examines the prospect of a sweeping Democratic victory. He argues that the party could achieve gains of a magnitude not seen since Barack Obama's historic presidential election in 2008. Johnson sees a combination of Democratic enthusiasm, and growing support among independents, white college-educated voters and Latinos, and signs of defections from Donald Trump's fiercely loyal electoral coalition.

item.title: WATCH: Remembering Patrick Stewart in his own words
item.description: As tributes pour in for Sir Patrick Stewart, World News Tonight remembers his interview with Diane Sawyer – sharing how theater became his safe space and his home.

item.title: Candy prices got you scared stiff? What to know about the cost of Halloween this year
item.description: Prices for candy, the most popular Halloween purchase, and gum have risen 7.7% in one year and are up more than 18% in two years, according to the latest federal data. (Image credit: Stephanie Scarbrough)

item.title: On what anatomical feature was Trump fixated this week? The quiz knows — do you?
item.description: Hint: He likes them big (and he cannot lie).

item.title: 2026 midterm election voter guides: Find local resources in your community
item.description: NPR member stations are gathering information for voters — from voter guides down to local races. Scroll through to find your state and the resources available from your local member station. (Image credit: David Ryder)

item.title: Websites pretending to be local news are boosting Democratic candidates
item.description: The websites of unknown origin are targeting key U.S. House races. They are getting picked up by ChatGPT's responses but Google's products avoid promoting them.

item.title: Nearly 2 out of 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots, new research shows
item.description: Most kids say they use chatbots for help with homework and when they're stressed, lonely, or anxious. And how they use chatbots is tied to their mental health. (Image credit: Matteo Della Torre)

item.title: Russia's bastion of free press Novaya Gazeta shuts down under Kremlin pressure
item.description: Newspaper Novaya Gazeta, one of the last vestiges of independent journalism in Russia, announced Friday that it was closing down, citing pressure from authorities who recently searched the home of its senior editor and earlier this year detained one of its journalists.

item.title: BP profits hit 18-year high as another bank makes billions
item.description: Profits at the UK-based oil and gas giant BP have hit an 18-year high, surpassing the level seen during the 2022 energy crisis.

item.title: Vote Republican, or else: How Trump is dangling government help on the campaign trail
item.description: President Donald Trump is signaling to states that his administration may be far less likely to help if their voters put Democrats in power on Election Day

item.title: 'I'm deeply hurt by the incompetence': Christa Pike releases statement after botched execution
item.description: Christa Pike, who survived an execution by lethal injection in the US, has spoken publicly for the first time since the incident a month ago and said she is in constant physical and mental pain.

item.title: Crypto industry suffers 'largest bank heist in human history'
item.description: Cryptocurrency worth more than $6.3bn (£4.7bn) has been stolen from a major exchange - with one industry insider telling Sky News it is "the largest bank heist in human history".

item.title: WATCH: What to know about health issues, rising costs on ballot in midterms
item.description: ABC News’ Devin Dwyer reports on the issues voters are weighing, and Cynthia Cox, senior vice president and director of KFF’s Program on the Affordable Care Act, discusses the ACA.

item.title: Ahead of midterms, backlash grows over soaring electricity bills
item.description: Nationwide, electricity costs have spiked approximately 5% in the past year, government data shows.

item.title: Top general fired from Pentagon's Joint Staff for alleged classified info leak
item.description: Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia is the latest senior military officer to be sidelined.

item.title: WATCH: See National Geographic's best destinations for 2026
item.description: ABC News' Sam Champion highlights some of the must-visit places featured on National Geographic's annual list of the world's best travel destinations.

item.title: WATCH: Obama slams Trump for getting mad at his Cheesecake Factory comment
item.description: The former president took issue with how President Donald Trump responded to his joke about "the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory."

item.title: FIFA to double Women's World Cup prize money - but it doesn't match men's tournament
item.description: FIFA plans to double Women's World Cup prize money next year but will not deliver on Gianni Infantino's ambition to match the cash paid out at the men's tournament, Sky News has learnt.

item.title: Watchdog investigating Met Police over handling of letter about Meghan's father
item.description: The Metropolitan Police is being investigated by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) over a letter containing allegations about the Duchess of Sussex's father, Thomas Markle Snr.

item.title: Why Google stock has plunged $500bn in a single day
item.description: Shares in Google's parent company Alphabet have suffered their worst-ever day on the US stock market, falling more than 12% and knocking around half a trillion dollars off its value.

item.title: WATCH: NICU babies dressed up for Halloween
item.description: The tiniest patients of the Cleveland Clinic Children's Hospital wear their first-ever Halloween costumes.

item.title: Leaflets promoting clinics in illegal Israeli settlements handed out at London medical recruitment event
item.description: Sky News has obtained copies of leaflets promoting medical clinics in illegal Israeli settlements by a company seeking to recruit British Jewish doctors at an event in London

item.title: Why defeated Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil for Miami - and what comes next
item.description: On Wednesday, Flavio Bolsonaro, who last week lost Brazil's presidential election, was seen arriving in the US on a private jet after having fled in the dead of night.

item.title: WATCH: Maine’s loggers and fishermen speak up about tariffs and higher diesel costs
item.description: ABC News’ Jay O’Brien talks to Maine Senate candidates Troy Jackson (D) and Sen. Susan Collins (R), as well as to fishermen and loggers impacted by tariffs placed on machinery imported from Canada.

item.title: WATCH: These dogs just love a pile of leaves
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a family from Maine that makes sure their yard always has a leaf pile ready for their two leaf-loving dogs.

item.title: WATCH: 'Liberty Biberty must go!' Protest over car insurance mascot
item.description: A small crowd took to the streets of Boston to protest against the existence of Liberty Biberty, the new fuzzy yellow mascot that appears in the insurance giant Liberty Mutual's TV ads.

item.title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles off east coast as tensions with South rise
item.description: North Korea has launched ballistic missiles off its east coast into the Sea of Japan, South Korea said on Thursday, as tensions continued to rise between the two countries.

item.title: WATCH: Long Island couple sues over real estate broker’s allegedly racist text
item.description: ABC News’ Linsey Davis speaks with a Long Island couple suing a now-former broker at realtor Douglas Elliman for housing discrimination, after the broker sent a text saying “Ugh they are black.”

item.title: WATCH: David Muir remembers the life and legacy of Barbara Barrie
item.description: The Oscar, Emmy and Tony nominee appeared in numerous films and TV series, including her role as the supportive mother in “Breaking Away.” David Muir remembers her legacy.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: Viral explorer finishes 500-mile paddle through Africa
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to Ash Dykes, an explorer who kayaked for 500 miles down the Congo Basin in Africa, paddling alongside monkeys and hippos.
